items.title: Bringing back creative research methods
items.summary: **What’s this session about?** Over the past decade, a quiet shift has happened. As research moved online, creativity got left behind. Semi-structured interviews became the default, and with them, we lost the richness and diversity of methods that help us uncover what people *really* think, feel, and do. Becky Mallaband and Rebecca Partridge are on a mission to change that. In this session, they'll share how a more creative approach to research (both in person and online) can help you go deeper, surface tacit knowledge, and get far more valuable insights from every session you run. items.summary: Your team releases faster with AI coding tools. But who checks what those tools leave behind? In this 45-minute online session I will take an app built with AI tools and break it live, step by step. You will see how API keys are pulled out of an installed app, how one user can read another user's data through a badly configured backend, and what an attacker finds in data stored on the phone. Then we turn it round: five checks you can ask your team to run on Monday, and the questions to ask before you sign off the next release. WHO IT IS FOR CTOs, technical founders, heads of engineering and product leads who are accountable for releases and customer data. This is not a beginner's coding clas…

items.summary: **What can you do with a DAX query? \| Zoe Douglas** Power BI has a query language to get data out of the semantic model -- the DAX query. This is different from DAX formulas you find in calculated columns, tables, and measures. With DAX query view you can quickly use this to understand your data, try out new formulas, and troubleshoot formulas you already have. If you were ever curious about what a DAX query was or want to know more, come and find out! **Zoe Douglas, Product Manager at Microsoft** I am a product manager for Power BI at Microsoft. I focus on unlocking awesome features for visuals and dedicated to helping all customers get the most out of their data!

items.summary: AI for DevOps & SRE: From Impressive Demos to Operational Trust What would make you trust an AI agent with operational changes? An agent can generate a valid command and still misunderstand the objective. It can mistake missing telemetry for a healthy service, or choose an action outside the scope you authorized. How do we recognize these failures before they affect real systems? Join Bucharest XDevOps Meetup for a practical, vendor-neutral session exploring the risks of AI-assisted operations and the controls that help manage them.
